newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chips end flat, electricals off.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chips end flat, electricals off.

text.p: Chilean blue chips seesawed through the afternoon to end almost exactly where they started as investors paid little heed to Wall Street's gains and focused instead on local electrical shares.
The selective IPSA index ended 0.02 percent lower to 97.65 points. The general IGPA ended 0.24 percent higher at 5391.81 points on very low volume of 4.9 billion pesos.
Brokers reported paltry turnover due to the two-day Fiestas Patrias holidays on Wednesday and Thursday. The bourse was due to close three hours early on Tuesday and Friday.
"It's really a two-day week. Pension funds and institutionals aren't buying very much," said one broker.
Brokers reported only a passing blip of interest in statements by new Central Bank President Carlos Massad, who said the bank will assess its restrictive credit policies daily.
Most electrical shares declined due partly to profit-skimming, including among the Chispa investment society stocks which rose last week on reports that Spain's Endesa plans to buy part of them.
Brokers said the price decline was only a speculative droop and that the market was still convinced Endesa of Spain would make its move.
"It's nothing negative, just the result of pure speculation," said a dealer at a large locally-owned brokerage.

The local daily El Mercurio reported Endesa was poised to begin buying up shares next week in the Chispa investment societies, which are owned by Enersis. Reports have said Enersis wants to sell part of the Chispas to raise money to bid in power privatizations in Brazil and elsewhere.
Chispa Dos slipped 0.8 percent to close at 178.51 pesos, while Enersis fell early and recovered to end unchanged at 253.50 pesos. Endesa Chile fell 0.6 percent to 258.50 pesos.
Risers included Campos, up one percent to 103 pesos, and Chilgener, up 0.6 percent to 2420 pesos.
Brokers said the bourse was likely to start seeing a long-awaited revival in October as speculation grows about third-quarter results and about a relaxation of interest rates.
